issues.description: Remedy: Taylor is entitled to the effective date he would have had absent the unconstitutional denial of access, which may be as early as September 7, 1971.
issues.quote: A veteran in Mr. Taylor's position is entitled, under ordinary remedial principles, to receive benefits for service-connected disabilities from the effective date that the veteran would have had in the absence of the government's challenged conduct.

issues.quote: the 'figurative handle' should be construed without the intent element as a figure, resemblance, or likeness which can be grasped by the hand.

issues.description: Discovery sanction: the district court excluded the late-produced assignment and imposed fees and costs for a continuance as a lesser sanction; the Federal Circuit found no abuse of discretion, favoring Infinity.
issues.quote: We cannot say that the district court abused its discretion by awarding the costs and fees.

issues.description: Attorney fees and costs awarded to Infinity as a discovery sanction for Sorrell's late production of the patent assignment, affirmed.

coding.author: Stoll

issues.description: Ongoing royalty order (equitable prospective remedy): Rule 60(b)(5) challenge to continuing royalties rejected, so the ongoing royalty stands.

issues.description: Trial and case management: denial of Rule 60(b)(2), (3), (5) and (6) motion to set aside the final judgment.

coding.case_type: Patent: district court and ITC

issues.description: Claim construction: the court held that for claim 27 the hollow hub is not part of the hollow drum, adopting Daktronics's construction and resolving a dispute the district court had left to the jury.
issues.quote: We agree with Daktronics that, with respect to claim 27, the claimed hollow hub is not a component of the claimed hollow drum.

issues.description: Literal infringement: the Vortek product does not literally meet element h because the hollow drum cannot receive the screw, so the final judgment of infringement is reversed.
issues.quote: The Vortek product does not literally meet element h of claim 27 because the hollow drum of the Vortek is not able to receive the screw.

issues.description: Mootness: the remainder of Daktronics's appeal and OSD's cross-appeal were dismissed as moot after the infringement judgment was reversed.
issues.quote: In view of this conclusion, we dismiss the remainder of Daktronics's appeal and the entirety of OSD's cross-appeal as moot.

coding.author: Prost
coding.notes: Unanimous panel. Lourie wrote separate additional views concurring in the result and reasoning; he was not a dissenter. The court reversed the final judgment of infringement, so the willfulness, fee, and other trial rulings were not reached and are not coded. Claim construction was coded by its effect on the judgment, which favored the accused infringer.

coding.case_type: Patent: district court and ITC
coding.side_b_parties: Leader Accessories LLC (accused infringer, defendant-appellant) and Jen-Feng Lee (its counsel, appellant)

issues.description: Contempt finding and sanctions for allegedly violating a protective order by disclosing confidential documents to a joint-defense counterpart; the court held the disclosure was not a clear violation given a fair ground of doubt, so the contempt finding was reversed.
issues.quote: We conclude that it was improper to hold Leader and Mr. Lee in contempt because, when read in context, there is a fair ground of doubt as to whether the protective order barred Mr. Lee's disclosure to develop a joint defense strategy.

issues.description: Award of attorney's fees and a $1,000 sanction against Leader following the contempt finding; the court reversed the award because the contempt finding lacked evidentiary support.
issues.quote: we reverse the district court's contempt order and its corresponding award of sanctions and attorney's fees.

coding.author: Dyk
coding.notes: Appeal is from a district court in a patent case, but the only issues decided concern civil contempt and sanctions for violating a protective order, not patent validity or infringement; the merits of the underlying infringement judgment were not at issue. The court applied Seventh Circuit law on sanctions review and Taggart's fair-ground-of-doubt standard. Judge Reyna dissented, arguing for deference to the district court and that the disclosure violated the protective order regardless of later misuse by a nonparty. The court also reviewed and rejected the first contempt theory (liability for the nonparty's disclosure), which was conceded as erroneous, and rested reversal on the second theory (joint-defense use).

issues.description: Applicant forfeited separate arguments against the obviousness rejection of claims 12 and 13 (Giamalva, Adams and Takakura) by not raising them before the Board.

coding.author: Taranto

coding.author: PER CURIAM
coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition. Appeal from the Court of Federal Claims (Judge Carolyn N. Lerner), No. 1:20-cv-00086. Affirmed in full. The Court did not reach the second and third Carmichael elements. Counsel withdrawal motion noted in a footnote is not coded as an issue.

coding.side_b_parties: United States

issues.description: Jurisdiction: whether the Claims Court had jurisdiction over a tax refund suit filed after the two-year limit of 26 U.S.C. 6532(a)(1), including whether the 7502 mailbox rule applied.
issues.quote: We therefore hold that the Claims Court correctly found that it lacked jurisdiction over Ms. Weston's 2012 and 2013 refund claims because she did not file her complaint within two years of the IRS disallowing those claims.

issues.description: Timeliness: whether the complaint was timely filed under the two-year limitations period of 26 U.S.C. 6532(a)(1), with the mailbox rule of 7502 held inapplicable to filings in the Court of Federal Claims.
issues.quote: Since Ms. Weston's complaint was a document filed not with the Tax Court, but with the Claims Court, the mailbox rule of § 7502(a)(1), where the postmarked, mailing date is deemed to be the filing date, does not apply.

coding.author: PER CURIAM
coding.notes: Nonprecedential per curiam affirming dismissal of a pro se tax refund suit for lack of jurisdiction as untimely. The Government's alternative 6511(b)(2)(A) argument was not reached (footnote 1) and is not coded. No dissents or separate opinions.

issues.description: Likelihood of confusion under section 2(d) based on DuPont factors for Tiger Lily's beer, spirits, bar and restaurant services applications.

coding.author: Lourie
coding.notes: Affirmed-in-part and dismissed-in-part. Tiger Lily's appeal of the Board's sustained oppositions and dismissal of its own opposition was affirmed; Barclays' cross-appeal was dismissed. The court did not reach Barclays' alternative grounds (false suggestion, dilution) because it affirmed on likelihood of confusion. Abandonment is coded under T01 because it was decided as part of priority in a section 2(d) opposition, not as a cancellation ground. Bona fide intent has no matching code, so it is coded X99. No judge dissented.

coding.case_type: Other Court of Federal Claims (takings, tax, military pay, vaccine, misc.)

issues.description: Spoliation: the Claims Court applied an incorrect control standard (requiring physical possession) in finding no spoliation of evidence other than the Hi-Point .380 handgun; vacated and remanded for a new spoliation determination.
